findings.title: Content Security Policy disabled (set to null)
findings.description: CSP is explicitly set to null, disabling all Content Security Policy protections. This allows inline scripts, eval(), and unrestricted resource loading, significantly increasing XSS attack surface.
findings.impact: Full XSS exploitation possible if any frontend vulnerability exists. No protection against inline script injection, data: URIs, or external resource loading.
findings.recommendation: Set a strict CSP policy. Example: "csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:;"
findings.fix: Replace null with a restrictive CSP string in tauri.conf.json

findings.title: Symlink resolution not validated - path traversal via symlinks
findings.description: The project_path function validates against '..' and absolute paths using Component::Normal check, but does NOT resolve symlinks. An attacker who can create symlinks inside the project directory (e.g., via compromised build process, supply chain, or social engineering) can escape the project root.
findings.impact: Arbitrary file read/write outside project directory. On Linux/macOS, symlinks can be created by any user. On Windows, requires admin but possible via junction points.
findings.evidence: project_path uses Path::components() with Component::Normal only, no canonicalize() or symlink resolution
findings.recommendation: After path construction, canonicalize the result and verify it starts with the canonicalized project root. Use std::fs::canonicalize() on both base and target paths.
findings.fix: Add symlink resolution validation in project_path: let canonical_base = fs::canonicalize(&base)?; let canonical_target = fs::canonicalize(&target)?; if !canonical_target.starts_with(&canonical_base) { return Err(...); }

findings.title: write_project_asset validation bypassable via symlinks
findings.description: The command validates that rel starts with 'resources/' but then passes to project_path which doesn't resolve symlinks. A symlink at resources/evil -> /etc/passwd allows writing arbitrary files.
findings.impact: Arbitrary file write outside project resources directory via symlink traversal
findings.evidence: Line 88: if !rel.starts_with("resources/") - only string prefix check, no filesystem validation
findings.recommendation: After project_path returns, canonicalize the target and verify it's within the canonicalized project_root/resources directory
findings.fix: Add canonicalization check after project_path call in write_project_asset and read_project_asset

findings.title: TOCTOU race condition in write_project_file and write_project_asset
findings.description: Both functions check if target exists (line 58, 102), then perform rename operations. Between the check and the rename, an attacker could replace the target with a symlink pointing to a sensitive file, causing the rename to overwrite that file.
findings.impact: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink race. On Linux/macOS where symlinks are easy to create, this is exploitable.
findings.evidence: Lines 58-75: had_target = target.exists() -> fs::rename(&target, &backup) -> fs::rename(&tmp, &target). Lines 102-105: similar pattern without backup.
findings.recommendation: Use atomic write with O_EXCL flag or verify target is not a symlink before each filesystem operation. On Unix, use open with O_CREAT | O_EXCL. Consider using tauri-plugin-fs with safe APIs.
findings.fix: Add symlink check before rename: if target.is_symlink() { return Err(...) } or use std::fs::OpenOptions with create_new(true) for atomic creation

findings.title: No symlink validation before file writes in any command
findings.description: None of the file write commands check if the target path is a symlink before writing. An attacker with ability to create symlinks in the project directory can redirect writes to arbitrary locations.
findings.impact: Arbitrary file write via symlink. Combined with SEC-004 race condition, high risk.
findings.evidence: No fs::read_link() or metadata().file_type().is_symlink() checks before writes
findings.recommendation: Add symlink check before any write operation: let meta = fs::metadata(&target)?; if meta.file_type().is_symlink() { return Err("Target is a symlink".into()); }
findings.fix: Add symlink validation helper function and call it before all write operations

findings.title: ZIP extraction doesn't validate extracted symlinks
findings.description: Both ZIP extraction functions use entry.enclosed_name() which prevents path traversal in ZIP entries, but don't validate if extracted entries are symlinks. A malicious ZIP could contain symlinks that, when extracted, point outside the temp directory.
findings.impact: Symlink extraction could lead to arbitrary file write/read outside temp directory during subsequent operations
findings.evidence: Lines 203, 322: entry.enclosed_name() prevents traversal but entry.is_symlink() not checked. Lines 209-218, 330-339: symlinks would be extracted as-is.
findings.recommendation: Reject ZIP entries that are symlinks, or extract them safely by resolving and validating target is within temp directory
findings.fix: Add check: if entry.is_symlink() { return Err("Symlinks not allowed in ZIP".into()); } before extracting each entry

findings.title: Insufficient input validation on project_exists command
findings.description: The project_exists command takes a dir parameter and directly joins with 'project.json' without validating the dir parameter for path traversal or symlinks.
findings.impact: Path traversal to check existence of arbitrary files on filesystem (information disclosure)
findings.recommendation: Apply project_path validation to dir parameter, or at minimum validate it's a valid directory path without traversal
findings.fix: Add validation: if Path::new(&dir).is_absolute() || dir.contains("..") { return false; } or use project_path pattern

findings.title: Capabilities could be more restrictive
findings.description: The default capability includes core:default which grants broad permissions. While dialog:default and window permissions are reasonable, core:default includes many permissions that may not be needed.
findings.impact: Over-privileged frontend - if compromised, has access to more Tauri APIs than necessary
findings.recommendation: Replace core:default with explicit minimal permissions needed: core:app:allow-exit, core:window:allow-close, etc. Use principle of least privilege.
findings.fix: Audit which core APIs are actually used and grant only those specific permissions

findings.title: Windows-specific rename handling incomplete for symlink protection
findings.description: Code handles Windows rename differently (lines 56-75) but doesn't account for Windows junction points or symlinks. On Windows, symlinks require admin but junctions don't. The backup/rename logic could be exploited via junctions.
findings.impact: Potential junction point attack on Windows to redirect file writes
findings.evidence: Windows-specific comment line 56-57, but no junction/symlink check
findings.recommendation: Add cross-platform symlink/junction detection using metadata().file_type().is_symlink() and on Windows also check for reparse points
findings.fix: Add platform-aware symlink/junction validation before rename operations

findings.title: Outdated dependencies with known vulnerabilities
findings.description: tauri 2.12.3 and tauri-plugin-dialog 2.8.2 may have known vulnerabilities. Should audit with cargo audit.
findings.evidence: tauri = "2.12.3", tauri-plugin-dialog = "2.8.2" - current latest may be higher
findings.recommendation: Run cargo audit regularly. Update to latest patched versions. Add cargo-audit to CI pipeline.
findings.fix: Update Cargo.toml dependencies to latest secure versions and run cargo audit
